multi-agent-research.label: Multi-agent research
multi-agent-research.description: Researcher gathers facts, Analyst distills them, Writer produces the final brief. Free — no key needed.

brainstorm-decide.label: Brainstorm & decide
brainstorm-decide.description: Optimist pitches ideas, Skeptic stress-tests them, Decider commits to one plan. Free — no key needed.

prompt-to-image.label: Prompt → Image
prompt-to-image.description: A free text model writes a vivid image prompt, then feeds an Image node. Type your idea and run.

compare-two-models.label: Compare two models
compare-two-models.description: One question, two models answer side by side, a judge picks the winner. Model B defaults to Bankr/Claude.

rag-over-folder.label: RAG over a folder
rag-over-folder.description: Pick a folder, ask questions — the agent searches your files and answers with citations. Needs a Bankr key.

summarize-url.label: Summarize a URL
summarize-url.description: Paste a link into the Text node — a web-enabled agent fetches the page and summarizes it. Needs a Bankr key.

geo-audit.label: GEO audit (answer-engine optimization)
geo-audit.description: Paste a page and the questions you want to win — the flow simulates how an answer engine would use it, then grades it and lists the fixes. Free — no key needed.

agentic-studio.label: Agentic Studio (multi-provider · debate → image + video)
agentic-studio.description: A creative team that ARGUES, then creates. A Bankr agent pitches, an OpenGateway agent critiques, a Surplus agent directs — then a Prompt node writes the image prompt (Surplus image) and a Scenarist scripts a video (Surplus video). Different providers, models, MCP/web tools and permissions per agent. Needs Bankr + OpenGateway + Surplus keys (funded Surplus key for media). Showcase / testing board.

storyboard.label: Storyboard (chained scenes · local)
storyboard.description: Chained scenes: a still opens the story, scene 1 animates it, and scene 2 starts from scene 1's LAST FRAME — the app extracts that frame for you. Type your premise, pick your local models, then Run flow. Honest limits: each scene is a separate ~5 s render and a full pixel round-trip, so colour and identity drift accumulate as the chain grows, and every scene pays its own model load. Think storyboard of a few scenes, not a long film.

prompt-to-image.label: Prompt → Image
prompt-to-image.description: A free text model authors a vivid image prompt, then feeds it into an Image node. Type your idea in the Prompt node, Run it, then Run the Image node (needs a Surplus key).

viral-video.label: Prompt → Viral → Video
viral-video.description: Concept writer drafts an idea, a Viral rewriter turns it into a kinetic text-to-video prompt, then it feeds a Video node. Free to author; Video gen needs a Surplus key.

improve-prompt-image.label: Improve prompt → Image
improve-prompt-image.description: Paste a rough image prompt into the Prompt node — a free text model polishes it and feeds an Image node. Run the Prompt node, then the Image node.

expert-roundtable.label: Expert roundtable (multi-agent chat)
expert-roundtable.description: Frontend, Backend & SEO experts brainstorm in turn — each builds on the last — then the CEO synthesizes the plan. Edit each agent's Instructions to customize the persona, or click "Add expert". Open "Chat with flow" to talk to the team.

code-helper.label: Code helper (files)
code-helper.description: One agent (Bankr/Claude) that reads & writes files in a folder you choose. Pick a folder, then run.

build-review.label: Build & Review (files, multi-agent)
build-review.description: Builder (Bankr/Claude) writes files in your folder, then Reviewer checks them. Pick a folder, then run.

writer-reviewer.label: Writer to Reviewer
writer-reviewer.description: Writer drafts, Reviewer critiques and improves it.

research-summarize.label: Research to Summary
research-summarize.description: Researcher gathers points, Summarizer condenses them.

code-review.label: Code to Review
code-review.description: Coder writes the code, Reviewer checks it for bugs.

howto.title: How to build a workflow
howto.restoreTitle: Remove the example and put your canvas back
howto.keepTitle: Keep the example on the canvas
howto.restoreNote: Your canvas is restored when you close — unless you choose "Keep example".

intro.title: What is a workflow?
intro.body: A workflow is a chain of AI steps you wire on this canvas — text, prompts, images, video, music. I will build a simple two-step example right in front of you; press Next and watch. (Every step you run drops its result as a card on the canvas you can branch from.)

provider.title: Step 1 — Provider
provider.body: A Provider is where the AI models come from. We are using the keyless FreeLLM router — no key needed. Every agent needs a provider for its "brain".

agent.title: Step 2 — Agent
agent.body: An Agent does the actual work. This one is the Writer. On the real canvas you add nodes from the palette on the left (drag one out).

wire.title: Step 3 — Wire them up
wire.body: Connect the Provider to the Writer by dragging from the edge of one node to the other. Now the Writer has a brain (its model). The wire just appeared.

second.title: Step 4 — Add a second step
second.body: Add a second Agent (Reviewer) and connect Writer to Reviewer. The label on that wire ("needs review") is a routing hint — it tells the flow when to move on. You now have a 2-step workflow.

run.title: Step 5 — Run it
run.body: That is a complete workflow. Click the highlighted "Run flow" button (glowing now), then "Run all" to run every node in order. Each step drops a result card on the canvas — branch a new node off any card to keep going, or hit the card's Regen to re-roll it.

beyond.title: Beyond agents
beyond.body: The palette has more: a Text node (a topic/brief), a Reference Image node (feed a character or style), Media nodes (image, video, music, TTS, STT — via Venice or Surplus), and a Prompt node that can SEE a wired image (vision). Any provider works — Venice, Bankr, Ollama, llama.cpp — with model capability tags shown inline. Save canvases in the Flows list on the left and switch between them like chats.

runPanel.title: Run Flow
runPanel.initialPlaceholder: Optional — leave blank to just run the flow. Prompt nodes carry their own instructions.
runPanel.runAllTitle: Run every node ONCE, top to bottom in dependency order (Prompt → Prompt → Media). Each node's output feeds the next — the whole pipeline on one click.
runPanel.stopTitle: Stop the run after the current node finishes (there is no mid-node abort).
runPanel.runNetworkTitle: Alternative: one shared agent-kit Network pass (agents share state — for roundtables). Uses the initial message above. Chained Prompt→Prompt may come back empty on some providers.
runPanel.idleAfter: to execute every node once, in dependency order — each node's output flows into the next, and the canvas fills in live. (The message box below only feeds the optional "Run as one network" mode.)
runPanel.runningNode: Running node {{step}} of {{total}}{{label}}… (watch the canvas — each node fills in as it finishes)
runPanel.noAgentOutput: The flow ran but produced no agent output.
runPanel.budgetTitle: Stop the run before the estimated spend crosses this many dollars. Empty = no cap. Estimates use each node’s wired model rates; local models are free.

chatPanel.title: Chat with flow
chatPanel.empty: Send a message — every expert in the flow weighs in (each builds on the previous one), and the MAIN agent synthesizes the decision. All takes are shown; the conversation is remembered across turns. Tip: load the "Expert roundtable" template or click "+ Add expert", and mark a node "MAIN" to choose who synthesizes.
